content.title: About
content.content: Hard pretzels with cheese filling are baked snack sticks shaped into traditional knots, made from wheat flour, salt and yeast, and filled with melted cheese. They have a crunchy crust, a soft interior and a rich cheesy flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pretzels originated in Europe where they were traditionally twisted into knot shapes.
The cheese filling often blends cheddar with processed cheese for a distinctive aroma.
Hard pretzels are commonly served as a snack with beer and fast‑food meals.
In the United States more than 200 million packages of pretzels are sold each year.
One legend says the knot shape symbolizes crossed hands in prayer.

items.title: Source of carbohydrates
items.content: Pretzels provide quick‑release carbs that supply energy for active tasks.

items.title: Protein content
items.content: The cheese filling adds a modest amount of dairy and plant protein.

items.title: Calcium from cheese
items.content: The cheese layer contributes calcium, important for bones and teeth.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Wheat flour contains B1, B2 and niacin, supporting metabolism.

items.title: Iron
items.content: Pretzels can help maintain iron levels in the body.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Pretzels made from wheat flour may trigger reactions in people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High sodium
items.content: The salty crust makes the product high in sodium; those with hypertension should limit intake.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Cheese filling raises the calorie count, so portions should be moderate.

items.title: Lactose
items.content: The cheese may contain lactose, which is relevant for lactose‑intolerant individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Pretzels are convenient as a standalone snack, paired with dips (cheese, mustard, tomato) or added to salads and soups for crunch.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in a sealed package in a cool, dry place. For longer storage, refrigerate to maintain crispness and prevent staling.
